rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (score 675.4, best so far). The oval finished 20/20 (max_error 0.014) and the s-bend 20/20 (max_error 0.022). The slalom still finished 0/20: progress 0.36, 1.8 line-loss events per run, and max_error at the 0.064 m off-track limit. So the remaining failure is excursion at the slalom's sharp direction changes. Iteration 8 also made the s-bend finish rate recover to 1.00 from 0.75 in iteration 7, which shows that y = 0.06 helps. The slalom is the only track that fails, and every earlier test that changed one geometry parameter (span, footprint, forward position) had side effects on the other tracks. Lowering base_speed (iteration 6) did not help the slalom. This iteration therefore changes one controller variable: kd from 0.8 to 1.0. The slalom's line losses and off-track events come from the loop reacting too slowly at sharp turns, and extra derivative action should damp the swing as the robot enters a bend. Geometry, base_speed, kp, ki and line-loss handling are held at the iteration 8 values, so any change in slalom progress and line losses can be attributed to kd. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events below 1.5 and progress above 0.4, with oval and s-bend completion held at or near 1.0. Hypotheses: (a) the slalom limit is loop damping at bend entry, so kd 1.0 cuts its line losses; (b) if steering_oscillation on the oval rises above 0.3 and the oval finish rate falls, derivative noise is now the limit and kd should return to 0.8 or be tried at 0.9; (c) if slalom line losses stay near 1.8, the limit is kp or sensor span, and the next test should widen the span to about 0.03 m alone. Measurements wanted next: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus control_effort to check steering load.
